readme.html:
Claude Shorts Skills

English · Bahasa Indonesia

Four Claude Code skills for making vertical short videos (YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Reels) on your own PC: animated 3D story shorts, word-synced captions, Minecraft short scripts, and code-driven Minecraft story videos. The repo also includes the Minecraft render engine those videos use. No AI video generator: the picture is rendered with three.js inside Remotion.

Made with these skills

Click a clip to watch the full short on YouTube.

Every frame is rendered on a home PC with three.js inside Remotion; no AI video generator, no stock footage.

The skills

Skill What it does
cartoon-3d-short 55-70 s vertical cartoon story shorts: 2D characters in a 3D world. Script formulas, voice-over, shot plan, camera, acting presets, sound mix, QA review agents and the final render. Looks: painted, PBR, paper diorama, Minecraft voxel.
captions Word-synced captions as a separate green-screen (and optional ProRes 4444 alpha) clip for After Effects, timed to the narration and kept clear of the Shorts UI.
minecraft-shorts Minecraft short scripts in English and Indonesian with two formulas ("What happens if...?" and the "how you built X" evolution ladder), an in-game test list and a Replay Mod shot list.
minecraft-story 2:15 "In this world / In this town" Minecraft story videos, built code-first: formula analysis, script and originality check, then one of two render paths. Default path (R): the whole video renders in Remotion with the Minecraft engine, so no game runs: VO lock, a one-world shotlist, parallel build agents, per-section keying with a numeric staging gate, review, sound, 2K 60 fps. Optional path (P1): takes in the game over RCON + Scarpet, recorded with ReplayMod, with per-agent file ownership enforced by a PreToolUse hook. Docs are in Indonesian.

Minecraft engine

engines/minecraft is the voxel renderer behind the Minecraft videos above: blocks, mobs, 70+ acting moves, cameras, water/lava, particles and the post look, drawn with three.js in Remotion. It comes with a set validator/stager, a numeric keying gate and a small demo.

It ships without any Minecraft textures. You extract them from your own copy of Minecraft Java Edition (python -I tools/mc_extract.py --jar <your .jar>), and they stay on your PC. Quick start and requirements are in its README.

Install

Step-by-step guide for beginners (Windows): README.id.md (Indonesian).

  1. Clone this repo.
  2. Copy the skills you want into ~/.claude/skills/:
    cp -r skills/* ~/.claude/skills/
    For minecraft-story, also install its sub-agents with node ~/.claude/skills/minecraft-story/scripts/install.mjs and start a new Claude Code session.
  3. Install the tools the video skills use: Node 20+, Remotion with @remotion/three, Python 3 and ffmpeg.
  4. In Claude Code, ask for example: "Use the cartoon short skill and make a short about the first elevator brake."

macOS

The skills were built and tested on Windows 11. The steps below should work on macOS, but have not been tested there yet: if something breaks, please report it in issue #5.

In Terminal:

# 1. Homebrew (skip if you have it), then the base tools
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
brew install git node python ffmpeg

# 2. Claude Code (run `claude` once and log in)
npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

# 3. + 4. Get the skills and copy them into Claude's folder
git clone https://github.com/fahniazz/claude-shorts-skills
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r claude-shorts-skills/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/
node ~/.claude/skills/minecraft-story/scripts/install.mjs   # only for minecraft-story

# 5. A Remotion project to render in
npx create-video@latest
cd my-video
npm install @remotion/three three @react-three/fiber
claude

Rendering uses Remotion's own browser unless you set CHROME_PATH, and the caption script picks Arial Black (or DejaVu Sans Bold on Linux) by itself; pass --font to use another font.

Settings

Variable Used for
REMOTION_TMP Temp folder for Remotion bundles; put it on a big drive (defaults to the system temp folder).
CHROME_PATH Optional Chrome/Chromium for rendering. If unset, the scripts use Chrome's usual Windows install when it exists, otherwise Remotion's own downloaded browser.
ELEVENLABS_API_KEY Optional AI voice (templates/scripts/eleven_voice.py). Put it in your project's .env; never commit it.
HF_CACHE_DIR Optional cache folder for the faster-whisper model used for word timings.
<ASSETS_DIR> In the docs, the folder where you keep your own asset kits (for example Kenney CC0 models).

Rules the skills follow

  • Story, characters and voice are your own. References are for measuring the look, never for copying content.
  • Sound effects are recorded (CC0 / free-licence), not synthesised.
  • Characters and captions stay inside the YouTube Shorts safe zone.

Contributing

Pull requests are welcome. Start with a good first issue and read CONTRIBUTING.md.

Credits

cartoon-3d-short started from the MIT-licensed skill by Mr omi (see skills/cartoon-3d-short/LICENSE) and was extended here with the diorama and Minecraft looks, an AI director, motion presets, a recorded-SFX audio pipeline, review agents and lessons from shipped shorts. Third-party reference frames from the original package are not included in this repo.

Minecraft is a trademark of Mojang Synergies AB. This project is not affiliated with Mojang or Microsoft.
